title: “My Oasis” (Sam Smith ft. Burna Boy) — UK is Silver, not Gold
was: UK Gold on the release row, in the dated log under 2025, and in the home page's tier bars (96 Gold · 30 Silver).
body: BPI's own register, title page for the single: “Most Recent Certification Silver · 22 August 2025 · Certification history: 22 August 2025 Silver”. One award, no Gold row.
now: Silver everywhere. Tier split is 95 Gold · 31 Silver; the 234 total and 26 countries are unchanged. The July 2026 bump to Gold had come from a typed event list, not the register — the worklist row now carries the BPI quote and read date.
guard: tests/handoffTotals pins 7 / 101 / 95 / 31 with a dated comment.

title: “Last Last” in France went straight to Diamond — there was no Platinum step
was: Dated log, 2023: “Last Last · SNEP 🇫🇷 Platinum”.
body: SNEP's register holds one row for the song: “Diamant · Date de constat 02/11/2023”. Other titles show their Or → Platine steps, so a Platine row would be visible if it existed.
now: The 2023 event is the Diamond itself.

title: “Last Last” in New Zealand — 2× Platinum in 2023, with Gold and Platinum in 2022
was: One 2023 row, “Platinum”, and no 2022 rows at all.
body: RMNZ's register (RadioScope): Gold 2022-09-08 · Plat ×1 2022-12-08 · Plat ×2 2023-12-21 · Plat ×3 2026-03-05.
now: 2023 reads 2× Platinum; the Gold and first Platinum are logged as 2022 events. The 2026 3× row was already there.

title: Love, Damini's Dutch Gold is a 2022 award
was: Logged under 2023.
body: NVPI's database: “Love, Damini · Album · Goud · 3-11-2022”.
now: Moved to 2022.

title: Three award events the registers hold that the dated log did not
was: “We Pray” UK logged only at Silver (2025); Love, Damini UK logged only at Silver (2023); “Alone” France absent from the log — though all three sat on the release rows already.
body: BPI: We Pray “01 May 2026 Gold · 10 January 2025 Silver”; Love Damini “01 December 2023 Gold · 10 February 2023 Silver”. SNEP: “ALONE · Or · Date de constat 26/10/2023”.
now: Three rows added. 2026 now logs 58 international awards (66 with Nigeria); 2023 logs 44. The year chips, the “New in 2026” strip and the “previous best” note all derive from the log and moved with it.

title: The dated log named the wrong certifying body for “Dai Dai” in Colombia
was: Release row said Sony Music Colombia; the 2026 log row said Pro Musica Colombia — two bodies for one plaque, on both layouts.
body: Repo data: the release cert carries a body override the log renderer ignored.
now: Both renderers honour the override. A test asserts every log event whose release cert overrides the body carries the same override.

title: The sources line was typed, out of date and named a body that no longer exists
was: “…BEA (Belgium)… cross-checked against Wikipedia's cited certification tables, as of August 2026” — nineteen bodies, missing Greece, Colombia, Hungary, Czechia and Slovakia.
body: BEA became BRMA in 2022 and publishes no register; Ultratop keeps the Belgian roster. Five bodies had been added to the data since the line was written.
now: Built from the COUNTRIES table by certSources(), dated by a CERTS_VERIFIED_ON constant (“most recently on 16 September 2026”).

title: Twelve “Dai Dai” week counts were a week or two behind the bodies
was: Global 200 14 weeks · Excl. US 15 · UK 14 · Sweden 16 · Germany 10 at No. 1 / 15 · Austria 11 / 15 · Italy 12 · Greece 6 / 12 · France 15 · Poland 13 · Luxembourg 14.
body: Each chart body's current issue, read 16 Sep: Billboard (12 Sep issue), Official Charts, Sverigetopplistan, Offizielle Deutsche Charts, Ö3, FIMI, IFPI Greece week 36, SNEP semaine 37, OLiS, Billboard Luxembourg.
now: 15 · 16 · 15 · 17 · 11/16 · 12/16 · 13 · 7/13 · 16 · 14 · 16. Luxembourg's No. 1 count stays at 8 with a floor note — Billboard serves no dated archive and the 5 September issue was never read. A maintainer's remark that had leaked into the rendered release note moved to a code comment.

title: Both Billboard global runs had ended, and the pages said they were still running
was: “retaken on the chart dated 22 August … and held since”; “a 10th consecutive week atop the Global 200 Excl. US”; “has not let go”. Same in Spanish.
body: Billboard Global 200 week of 12 Sep 2026: No. 1 Karol G, No. 3 “Dai Dai” (LW 1, 15 weeks). Global Excl. US: No. 2.
now: Written as closed in both languages and the story: seven weeks at No. 1 in all, the second spell being the issues of 22 and 29 August and 5 September; ten straight weeks atop the Excl. US, 4 July to 5 September.

title: Four more “Dai Dai” claims written in the present tense after their runs closed
was: Spotify weekly “in its 13th week”; “Big Top 40 for a 3rd week”; Rhythmic Airplay No. 1 on 5 September only, Pop Airplay “No. 27, one off the peak”; YouTube “has since retaken the top”.
body: Spotify Charts (weekly, 10 Sep chart); Big Top 40 issues of 9–30 August; Billboard Rhythmic Airplay 5, 12 and 19 September issues; YouTube Global Daily Top Music Videos dated 14 September (No. 2 behind a new entry).
now: Spotify weekly: six weeks at No. 1, run closed 27 August, 16-week stay through 10 September. Big Top 40: four weeks. Rhythmic: two weeks at No. 1 (5 and 12 Sep), No. 2 on 19 Sep; Pop Airplay No. 26 on 19 Sep, equalling its peak. YouTube: the second spell ended too, on the 14 September chart. The untracked “6.1 million likes” was dropped rather than refreshed.

title: Greece's upgrade had reached the data but not the typed prose
was: “Gold in Colombia, Greece, the Czech Republic, Italy & Poland”; story rail “Platinum in 5 more”; Spanish twin said the same.
body: IFPI Greece week 36/2026 chart, Award column: P.
now: Greece sits in the Platinum list in both languages; the rail note is counted from the certs array (“Platinum in 6 more” / “platino en 6 países más”) so the two editions cannot part again.

title: Spotify daily-chart read advanced a day
was: Streak 116, total 117, through the 14 September chart.
body: charts.spotify.com Daily Top Songs Global, 15 Sep 2026: No. 20, Streak 117, Total days on chart 118.
now: 117 / 118, confirmed through 15 September, with a feed entry.

title: The Headies 2026 — five nominations, not four
was: Four rows; a code comment excluded a fifth “Producer of the Year for Bundle by Bundle” as the producer's nomination; 241 nominations site-wide.
body: theheadies.com nominee cards, read one by one: “BURNA BOY / NO SIGN OF WEAKNESS / ALBUM OF THE YEAR” is the seventh card in that category. The body's Producer of the Year field is Magicsticks, P.Priime, Ragee, Sarz and Tempoe — no Bundle by Bundle. The producer nomination the press lists carried never existed at the body.
now: Album of the Year added; 242 nominations across 47 bodies. The comment now tells the real story.

title: AFRIMMA 2026 resolved at the body
was: A pending-results row: “body site down; no winners on its X or Instagram” (checked 14 Sep).
body: afrimma.com's home page, “AFRIMMA 2026 Award Winners — THE OFFICIAL RESULTS”, published 15 Sep 15:22 UTC: Artist of the Year Fally Ipupa; Album of the Year Davido, 5ive; Crossing Boundaries Fally Ipupa; Best Male West Africa Ruger. He is not named in any of the 41 honours.
now: Four losses recorded; the pending row removed.

title: The 200M-stream board was a month behind kworb
was: “No other African act has more than Tems's five” in the 300M tier; CKay tied on 3 with Wizkid and Omah Lay; “As of August 2026”.
body: kworb per-artist song tables, 15 Sep: Tyla has six songs past 300M (Water, PUSH 2 START, CHANEL, Truth or Dare, Show Me Love, Jump); CKay has four past 200M (the North African remix of love nwantiti is the fourth, a separate version the board's rule counts).
now: “The next-deepest is Tyla with six, then Tems with five”; CKay 4, alone; dated 16 September 2026.

title: ChartMasters equivalent-album-sales board re-read
was: Burna Boy 15.13M, Wizkid 14.85M, gap “some 284,000”, “691-name board”, “the only Afrobeats artists it has published an EAS total for at all”.
body: ChartMasters' own table (692 rows, sorted by Total EAS reproduces g#): Burna Boy 15,197,000 (534, stamped 14 Sep) · WizKid 14,887,000 (538, stamped 13 Sep) · Beéle 10,914,000 tagged Afrobeats, Colombia · Akon 16,620,000 (502).
now: 15.20M / 14.89M, gap some 310,000, 692 names. The source line discloses that the pair is NOT same-date (it flatters the gap by about a day of WizKid's streams). The “only Afrobeats artists” clause is gone; Beéle is named.

title: The phone's most-streamed board named Tems alone for 2026
was: Mobile row “01 Tems 🇳🇬 2026 · in progress” while the desktop, from the same data, marked Tems, Burna Boy and Wizkid joint first (within the count's ten-million resolution).
body: Repo: the mobile derivation read entries[0] and ignored the tie flags the data declares.
now: “Tems, Burna Boy & Wizkid · 2026 · in progress · joint”. tests/africaBoards pins it.

title: Undated running totals, a wrong platform, a wrong crowd and a wrong tour scope
was: Album totals (1.71B / 1.35B / 868M) printed with no date; 2027 London Stadium “announced on Instagram”; Lionesses parade “a 100,000-strong crowd”; Red Rocks “opening the No Sign of Weakness tour”.
body: kworb album table 15 Sep (1.73B / 1.39B / 878M — they drift daily); the announcement is x.com/burnaboy/status/2084371889254727698, 3 Aug 2026; the FA's own reports put the Buckingham Palace crowd at 65,000; Red Rocks opened the North American leg, not the tour.
now: Totals dated “as read on 22 August 2026”; “Announced by Burna Boy on X”; “a crowd the FA put at 65,000”; “opening the North American leg … (12 November 2025)” on both pages.

title: The conversion-rate note contradicted the Bugatti on the same page
was: “USD figures use each source's own conversion (~₦1,455/$)” — but the Bugatti's ₦9bn had been re-converted at ₦1,370.08/$ on 8 September.
body: Repo: every other current car divides to ₦1,428–1,500/$; the lead car, 39% of the headline total, did not.
now: The note derives both rates from the rows: “~₦1,460/$ … except the Bugatti Chiron, whose reported ₦9 billion is converted here at ₦1,370/$, the rate on the day the buy was announced”.

title: The French No. 1 run had closed and the feed never said so; one entry was out of order
was: The two 9 September entries read the run as live; a 12 September entry sat below an 11 September one.
body: SNEP Top Singles semaine 37 (11 septembre): “Dai Dai” No. 3, down from No. 1 — nine consecutive issues on top, semaine 28 to 36.
now: A closing entry; the feed reordered. tests/updatesOrder asserts the array never goes back up in date, since the home band, the digest and lastEntry all trust updates[0].

title: The live boards said “hourly” in forty places, and were not
was: “refreshed every hour” / “rebuilt hourly” / “Updated hourly” on the page, the phone lede, the meta description, the share card, the records hub, every artist's live page, the API docs, the search index.
body: GitHub Actions run history for stats-live.yml, 12–16 Sep: runs at 01:28, 06:51, 12:38, 17:18, 20:27 UTC on the 16th — every two to six hours — although the cron is “17,47 * * * *”. GitHub runs schedule events best-effort.
now: One constant, LIVE_CADENCE (“refreshed several times a day”), everywhere; the snapshot is stamped to the minute (“16 September 2026, 20:40 UTC”) on both layouts.
guard: tests/liveClaims refuses “hourly” or “every hour” in any rendered text under app/.

title: Share card and page disagreed on the country count
was: OG card “Charting in 151 countries right now”; page and meta “149 countries”.
body: Repo: the generated file counted raw kworb codes — “UK” and “GB” both present, “WW” counted as a country — while the page recounted with the site's rule.
now: The generator applies the rule; both say 149. A test holds the generated count to countriesOf().

title: Blank tinted squares where the phone had no cover art
was: Kainama and “Apple Music Live: Burna Boy” drew a monogram on desktop and an empty square on mobile.
body: Repo: the mobile row always set a background image, even when there was none.
now: The phone draws the release's initial in the desktop's tile style.

title: Two “single-show” grosses were halves of two-night totals
was: Rank 10 Scotiabank Arena, Toronto $1,400,964 and rank 23 Bell Centre, Montreal $952,192, tickets “Not reported”.
body: TouringData's I Told Them… Tour table prints one combined report per stand: “February 24-25, 2024 · Scotiabank Arena · $2,801,928 · 29,579 (100%) · 2 shows” and “February 28-29 · Centre Bell · $1,904,384 · 26,303 · 2 shows”. 2,801,928 ÷ 2 = 1,400,964 exactly. No per-night gross was ever published — and the headcount it did publish had been dropped.
now: Both rows withdrawn from the single-show ranking (board is 41 rows). Then, on Paul's question — the body has the figures, so why lose them — the two stands were put back beneath the board as what they are: Toronto $2,801,928 / 29,579 tickets over 2 nights, Montreal $1,904,384 / 26,303 over 2 nights, on both layouts and in the API, with no per-night split invented. A guard refuses a “1 of 2 nights” row without a headcount; another holds the stands to Boxscore's figures and off the ranked board.

title: Gurtenfestival 2024 — 18,000, not “over 80,000”
was: “Headlined before over 80,000 fans (18 July)”.
body: The organisers' own balance (neo1.ch, 23 Jul 2024): 73,000 entries across four days, capacity 20,000 a day; “am Donnerstag waren es deren 18'000”. He played the Thursday.
now: “Headlined the Thursday (18 July) before 18,000 — the organisers' own count for his night at a festival capped at 20,000 a day, which drew 73,000 entries over its four days”.

title: Sunny Hill's crowd figure had no body; the Ibiza show was missing
was: “before ~15,000” (a fan aggregator's number matching the OLD venue's ceiling); the O Beach Ibiza headline of 14 August 2026 was on the performance map and in the feed but not in the festivals list (58 total).
body: No body publishes a Sunny Hill 2024 count; KOHA's review dates his set to the second night, Friday 26 July. Ibiza Spotlight and welcometoibiza date the Luna Loca launch to Friday 14 August 2026.
now: Sunny Hill dated instead of counted; Luna Loca launch added (59 total).

title: “Two short-form releases, seven years apart” — they are three years apart
was: Typed “seven years apart” over EPs the same page dated 2016 and 2019.
body: Spotify's album pages: Redemption 23 September 2016; Steel & Copper 21 March 2019.
now: Derived from the EP years: “three years apart”.

title: The method card named four stream-ratio bodies while the table priced six
was: “Streams-based bodies — France, Denmark, Norway and the Netherlands — are converted with the body's own published download-equivalence” — yet Czech and Slovak plaques on the same page were priced by exactly that rule.
body: ČNS IFPI's rules PDF: “1 download = 222 subscription streamů”; the site had priced CZ and SK this way since the page launched.
now: Derived from CERT_THRESHOLDS with the filter the methodology page uses: “Czechia, Denmark, France, the Netherlands, Norway and Slovakia”. A render test holds the card to the data.

title: Finding 02 left Lebanon and India out of its own count
was: “…11 are not — Nigeria and South Africa, and a run through Latin America and the Gulf.”
body: Repo: the eleven non-European No. 1 countries include LB and IN, which the typed tail never mentioned.
now: “— Africa, Latin America, the Gulf, the Middle East and South Asia”, from a region map; a test fails on any non-European No. 1 country the map does not know.

title: Four sentences on the methodology page had drifted from the data they describe
was: “three of them changed figures” (four had); “Greece, Belgium, Colombia and the rest of the unpriced bodies publish no threshold” (Belgium's were found and priced on 10 Sep); “CAPIF (Argentina)” as an example body (no Argentine plaque on the site); BVMI “Albums did not move”.
body: BVMI's own guideline: album levels moved DOWN on 30 June 2023 to 75,000 / 150,000 for releases from that date.
now: Count and names derived; FIMI in place of CAPIF; the BVMI vintage note states both album bands. The Rhythmic dispute entry is dated and records both charts' later No. 1s.

title: 929M YouTube Music audience presented as current
was: “YouTube Music monthly audience — first African artist ever past 900 million”, no date, while the platform showed 875M.
body: The 929M is an all-time high read on 12 August 2026 (feed entry of that date).
now: “YouTube Music monthly audience, at peak — set 12 August 2026”, the same treatment the Spotify-listeners tile already had. Guarded.

title: Timeline and FAQ sentences written before the summer ended
was: About 2025: “on his biggest North American tour to date”; About 2026 stopped at the Opening Ceremony; FAQ: “has spent 37 days at No. 1 … reclaiming the top spot in August”; “his most-streamed track”.
body: tours.ts (world tour across Oceania, North America and Europe); the Final halftime show of 19 July and the Global 200 No. 1; Spotify's chart (the 37 days ran 30 June–22 August); Last Last is his most-streamed SOLO song.
now: Past tense and dated throughout; the 2026 row carries the Global 200 No. 1 and the halftime show.

title: The UK run written as live
was: “a 5th week at that peak, 14 weeks in” / “5.ª semana en ese pico, ya con 14 semanas en lista”.
body: Official Charts song page: peak 2, five weeks at No. 2 (30 Jul–27 Aug 2026), then 15, 14, 19 — 15 weeks through the chart of 17 September.
now: “five weeks at that peak, 30 July to 27 August 2026, in a 15-week stay counted through the chart of 17 September (No. 19)” — both languages.

title: Refuted — the home band's “37 days” is already the dated form
was: An auditor flagged “now spent 37 days as the most-streamed song on Earth — back on top in August” as live.
body: tests/liveClaims certifies that sentence's shape; the count is closed and dated.
now: No change.

title: Refuted — On a Spaceship is 19 tracks by the site's own rule
was: An auditor wanted 20, because Spotify lists 20.
body: Spotify's 20th is “Soke”, which the artist's own 2015 tracklist and every reference list as the sole bonus track; albums.ts states it counts standard editions, and applies that to L.I.F.E too.
now: No change.

title: Refuted — re-adding Toronto and Montreal as combined two-night rows
was: The auditor's option B: keep the rows at the body's combined grosses.
body: A $2.80M two-show report would rank 5th on a board titled highest-grossing SINGLE shows and feed the home page's top five.
now: Rows withdrawn instead (see above).
